Hyperparameters for tokenisation, pretraining, fine-tuning are shown in Table 8, Table 9 and Table 10, respectively. We did not use stochastic tokenisation (BPE-dropout or subword regularisation). Table 8: Hyperparameters for tokenisation.
ImplementationSentencePiece (Kudo and Richardson, 2018)
Vocabulary Size16000
BPE-dropout0
Unigram Subword Regularisation0
Table 9: Hyperparameters for pretraining.
Implementationfairseq (Ott et al., 2019)
ArchitectureRoBERTa (base) (Liu et al., 2019)
Precision16 bit
OptimizerADAM (Kingma and Ba, 2014), ε = 1e-6, β = (0.9, 0.98)
Sequence length512
Learning rate sched-ulerLinear warm-up for 10000 updates to 5e-4, then reduce to 1e-4 upon increased training loss at epoch
Training for100000 updates / 30 epochs
Batch size2048
Dropout0.1
Attention Dropout0.1
Weight Decay0.01
Table 10: Hyperparameters for finetuning.
Implementationfairoseq (Ott et al., 2019)
ArchitectureRoBERTa (base) (Liu et al., 2019)
Precision16 bit
OptimizerADAM (Kingma and Ba, 2014), ε = 1e-6, β = (0.9, 0.98)
Sequence length512
Learning rate sched-ulerLinear warm-up to 2e-3 for 6% of up-dates, then linear decay to 0
Training for20 epochs
Batch size32
Dropout0.1
Attention Dropout0.1
Weight Decay0.01

Pretraining was run on 8 NVIDIA Tesla V100s. We ran pretraining on the text of English Wikipedia. A Wikipedia dump was processed with the Python package WikiExtractor $^{10}$ , and then split into sentences using BlingFire $^{11}$ . In order to perform a fair comparison across models, we removed all sentences with sequence lengths longer than 510 when tokenised with the modified models including spaces. However, this was a very small amount

```txt
10https://github.com/attardi/wikiextra  
ctor/  
11https://github.com.microsoft/BlingFi  
re 
```

of the data $(\sim 0.002\%)$ and would therefore have a negligible effect on performance.

Loss curves are shown in Figure 3.

Finetuning was run on a single NVIDIA Tesla V100. All finetuning experiments were ran with a batch size of 32, and a peak learning rate of 2e-3 with linear warm-up for $6\%$ of updates, then linear decay to 0. All other parameters were kept the same as for pretraining. Experiments were ran for 20 epochs, and the best performing epoch was taken, with 10 random seeds per model. For the Superbizarre datasets, we took the best performing epoch for each seed on the dev set and evaluated it on the test set.
